chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: How the Palomar fire started
summary: The fire began from draperies touching footlight bulbs on the bandstand and destroyed all instruments and scores.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: The fire at the Palomar, that started in radio equipment, is that correct?
No, it started right on the bandstand.

Well, they had these draperies. It had been terrifically hot in L.A., you know, up in the hundreds, and everything was dried out, and these -- nowadays, of course, you couldn't hang draperies without the Fire Department checking them, you know, for being fireproof. And we had these huge electric light bulbs in the footlights back of there, and these curtains would sag, so one of them was touching one of these lights, and it just went phfffft, like that, and we were actually in the place. We were off the bandstand at the time, taking an intermission. And the fire went up so fast it was just like it exploded. It just went whoosh, like that, and the whole -- the only guy that got his instrument off was the bass player, who had laid it down on the front edge of the

apron. Because I always liked the bass up close to me, up front. Because as far as I'm concerned that's where it all comes from, the bass. Everything that's happening. And he was able to -- he got singed a little bit, but he got it off. Everything else was gone, all the instruments, all the music. We even had the trunk with the scores in it, because we were leaving. It was the next to the last night. And we had the trunk down there, all the scores that we had put into the band. Well, we had been gone from New York, maybe like three months. They were all in the trunk, and they went up too. So it was just like starting from scratch. But I always figured maybe somebody did me a favor there, because I had a whole mixed up bag of arrangements, and maybe they started me off, you know, with a clean slate, and I got rid of a lot of stuff that I shouldn't have been playing. And the ones that were important we were able to recreate.
